subject: Working with clusters and observation-level strata.

messages.author: b480b89888b88e0e
messages.subject: Working with clusters and observation-level strata.
parts:
Hi, I'm learning to use the distance package on R, but I haven't figured how to include some analysis details available on the Distance 7.3. I was wondering if I could get some help here.
Such details are...
  1. Using size-bias regression method for cluster size estimation.
    As I understand from this example, I just need to change my fromula to:
    formula = ~size or formula = ~log(size). Am I correct?
  2. Estimates resolution level: Global cluster size.
    Using the R package, apparently only mean cluster size per stratum is used. Is there a way to change this use the global mean cluster size for the density estimation on each stratum?
  3. Post-stratify, using: Observation.
    I'm insterested on the estimations of different strata at observation level (e.g. different species for a single survey with a shared detection function). Is this possible? I've got no problem stratifying by geographic regions/time, but I can't figure out how to stratify at observation level using the R package.
Thanks!

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Working with clusters and observation-level strata.
parts:
Eliphaleth

Thanks for the questions and happy you found the vignettes we have posted.  Now to your questions.

  1. Dealing with potential bias in density of individuals is indeed most readily accomplished by incorporating group size into the detection function.  This explicitly recognises that detectability is a function of group size as well as distance from the transect.  The approach described in the "group size" vignette that you reference does exactly that.
  2. There is not a way to select mean group size at the global level for stratum-level density estimates.  I'm not sure this is a good idea because if you want density estimates at the stratum level, it would seem that stratum-level mean group size would be the appropriate thing to use.
  3. There is a function dht2 released to CRAN in January that enables post-stratification at the observation level.  I don't think we have an example of its use on the examples web page, but have a look at the documentation for the dht2 function in the Distance package.  You can also get a clue from slide 15 of this talk: https://workshops.distancesampling.org/standrews-2019/intro/lectures/BlockG-stratification.pdf

Eric Rexstad

eric.r...@st-andrews.ac.uk
The Observatory, Buchanan Gardens, St Andrews KY16 9LZ
